description: Robert B. Jones, Jr. was appointed as a United States Magistrate Judge in 2007.  Prior to his  appointment, he practiced civil litigation in Raleigh and Wilmington.  His previous work included service  as a law clerk to Judge Boyce F. Martin, Jr., of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit in Louisville,  Kentucky.  After receiving his undergraduate degree from Davidson College, he obtained his law degree  from Campbell University School of Law.  Judge Jones is a member of the North Carolina Bar Association  Dispute Resolution Council.  He is also a member of the bar associations of North Carolina and New  Hanover County.  He is a former member of the Law-Related Education (LRE) Advisory Committee to the  North Carolina Bar Association, during which time he was a contributing editor of The North Carolina  Constitution Explained, a classroom guide for school teachers on the state constitution.                     Judge Jones maintains chambers in Wilmington.
summary: Robert B. Jones, Jr. is the United States Magistrate Judge and is currently active.

description: Upon his graduation from law school, Judge Numbers joined the Winston-Salem office of  a large North Carolina-based law firm.  From 2005 until 2010, Judge Numbers’ practice focused  on civil rights claims against local municipalities and government contractors.  In 2010, Judge  Numbers joined the firm’s Raleigh office and concentrated his practice on complex business  litigation in state and federal courts. He is admitted to all North Carolina state and federal courts,  the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals, the Third Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States  Supreme Court.   During his time on the bench, Judge Numbers has handled a variety of matters.  In the  criminal arena, he has conducted thousands of initial appearances and detention hearings as well  as dozens of bench trials.  With respect to civil matters, Judge Numbers has handled matters  addressing innumerable topics including, patent, copyright, civil rights, environmental issues, and  complex business disputes.  Judge Numbers is also the chair of the Court’s Local Patent Rules  Committee.  Judge Numbers’ chambers are located in Raleigh, North Carolina.

description: Kimberly A. Swank serves as a part-time United States Magistrate Judge with chambers  in Greenville.  She received her undergraduate degree from East Carolina University and  graduated cum laude from Campbell University School of Law in 1991.  She enjoys a varied  legal background, having served in the Office of Chief Counsel of the United States Secret  Service and having worked in private practice in Greenville prior to coming to the court in 2004.   While in private practice, she was primarily engaged in civil, criminal appellate and capital  habeas litigation.  From 2004 until the time of her appointment as a Magistrate Judge, she  worked with the court as a death penalty law clerk and career law clerk to the Honorable  Malcolm J. Howard, Senior United States District Judge.  She also served as a law clerk to the  late Louis B. Meyer, Associate Justice of the North Carolina Supreme Court from 1991 to 1992.   Throughout her career, Judge Swank has been actively involved in the bar, having previously  served as a member and Chair of the Executive Committee of the Conference of Bar Presidents  sponsored by the NC State Bar (2002-2013; Chair 2008-2009), President of the 3A Judicial  District Bar, (2001-2002), President of the Pitt County Bar Association (1998-1999) and member  of the Eastern North Carolina Inn of Court.  Judge Swank was sworn in to office on September  10, 2013.
summary: Kimberly A. Swank is the United States Magistrate Judge and is currently active.

description: James E. Gates of Raleigh took office as a Magistrate Judge of the U.S. District Court for  the Eastern District of North Carolina in January 2006.  He came to the court from a mid-sized  Raleigh-based law firm, where he practiced business litigation for twenty years and served on the  firm’s management committee.  His previous work included private practice in the District of  Columbia and service as a law clerk (1983-85) to U.S. District Judge Frank W. Bullock, Jr. (ret.)  of the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of North Carolina.  Judge Gates is a former  chair of the Dispute Resolution Section of the N.C. Bar Association (1998-99) and served on  numerous other bar committees.  He is also a former North Carolina-certified mediator.  After  receiving his undergraduate degree from Ursinus College (B.A. summa cum laude, 1977), he  obtained his law degree (1981) and a master’s degree in foreign service (1985) from Georgetown  University.  Judge Gates is one of two judges leading the court’s HOPE reentry program for  offenders with substance abuse problems, chairs the court’s Civil Rules Committee, and has been  a member of other court committees.  He is the principal author of the five-volume North  Carolina Civil Trial Guide (Matthew Bender) and has co-taught a class on federal practice and  procedure at Campbell University School of Law.  In April 2020, Judge Gates retired from full- time service, but continues to serve in a part-time, recall capacity.
summary: James E. Gates is the United States Magistrate Judge and is currently active.
